newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen stagnant before Wednesday's U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen stagnant before Wednesday's U.S. data.

text.p: Bunds stagnated in early trade on Monday and dealers predicted the market would stay confined to a range of 99.30-99.70 for the rest of the day, with little prospect of movement before a series of U.S. data on Wednesday.
December Bund futures were quoted at 99.54 at 0844 GMT, down one basis point from Friday's close, while the yield on the benchmark, 6.25 percent 10-year April bond remained unchanged at six percent.
Dealers said the market had settled after swinging last week as comments from Bundesbank officials caused confusion about whether the German rate cut cycle was over or not.
"The market is relatively stable, it looks like the repo rate will stay unchanged for the foreseeable future," one trader said.

Comments last Friday from Bundesbank council members Otmar Issing and Ernst Welteke suggested that the central bank may yet cut interest rates if conditions allowed, softening a stance taken only last Wednesday when Issing had said another rate cut was neither to be expected nor necessary.
"Explicit rate cut hopes are unlikely to return to the market soon," the research department at Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank said in a written commentary.
The dollar would have to depreciate well below 1.50 marks for hopes of an easing to revive, the bank said.
Dealers said Bunds had settled into a broad range of 99 to 100 for the time being.
The main focus of the week was likely to be Wednesday's set of U.S. data, dealers said.
Wednesday sees the release of preliminary U.S. GDP for the third quarter, new homes sales for September and the Federal Reserve's Beige Book on economic conditions.
Dealers said the data would help shape market opinion on the likelihood of an interest rate increase at the Fed's Open Market Committee Meeting on November 13.
